RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Has posted several solid efforts in defeat over hurdles, with best form coming at Clonmel; however, was pulled-up in a tongue-tie at Killarney last time but that is left off today so can rebound.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Runner-up on sole point start before winning a 2m bumper at this meeting last year on second rules start; was poor in soft ground in a Listed bumper on sole 2026 run but has to be respected back here on hurdles debut on good ground; penalised 8lb, though.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ran well at times in bumpers without winning, including here; some solid efforts in four maiden hurdles but has fallen once and didn't jump that well last time so needs to do better.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Modest form in bumpers and three maiden hurdles so handicaps will suit better after today.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Has shown some ability in bumpers and maiden hurdles but has been pulled-up in two points this year; has to return to best for a new yard with cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Second runner for yard; didn't progress in seven points and well beaten at Cork on hurdling debut so best watched today.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ran well enough before falling in a 3m Punchestown maiden hurdle two starts ago but was well beaten at Cork since; others preferred.

RaceName: Frank King Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Well beaten in a Killarney bumper on debut and can only be watched for the time being.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Second runner for yard; dual hurdle winner is rated 123 in that sphere; fine efforts in both chase starts including when just behind stablemate Future Prospect at Wexford last time; her previous Killarney run was over 2m5f so this trip should be fine; big player.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: One of three runners for yard; point, bumper and maiden hurdle winner fell on chasing debut at this venue but has been runner-up twice since at Wexford over 2m and 2m3f; just in front of stablemate La Note Verte last time; a big player if staying this trip.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Third runner for yard; point and bumper winner hit form over hurdles last year, winning twice and getting to a rating of 127; seems to be the stable third string on return/chasing debut but can still give a good account.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Bumper and dual hurdle winner is rated 121 in that sphere though disappointed when last seen in 2025; makes chasing debut for a new yard and is respected but ran poorly on her only run at this track last year.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Dual point winner won a Clonmel maiden hurdle over 2m4f last autumn; posted some fine runs in defeat after in Listed and Grade 3 company; has to be respected on chasing debut even after a break.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Point winner is a maiden over hurdles and rated only 86 in that sphere so has a lot to find on chasing debut.

RaceName: Victoria House Tramore Mares Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Maiden is rated only 77 over hurdles so can't be fancied in this company on chasing debut.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Hurdle winner has twice run well in defeat at this track over fences this year, including over C&D; unseated at Galway last time but has a squeak on those better earlier runs.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Hurdle winner ran well enough on h'cap chase debut at Punchestown but was poor over hurdles last time at Ballinrobe; the cheekpieces worn then are left off today so he could rebound.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual chase winner was second over hurdles at Killarney in May and ran a cracker back over fences at Galway last time; looks a big player down 2lb and in grade.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Three hurdle wins; dual chase winner at Thurles; ran well enough at Galway last time but needs to do more today even dropped 2lb.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
OwnerName: Pat Tennyson & N P Morrissey & Raymond Micheal Cody
Spotlight: Won this race last year but has been mostly below form this year over hurdles and fences; is still 3lb above last year's winning mark so has to return to best.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Dual chase winner has run well in defeat at this track; however, was pulled-up on his last chase run and below form over hurdles since so others preferred.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Point winner has only had six runs under rules; promising Kilbeggan chasing debut but not as good twice since; however, can do better again now entering handicaps.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner here; both chase wins came at Kilbeggan when with Henry de Bromhead; below form last four starts and needs a return to his best.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner won a Galway beginners' chase last year but hasn't been as good since; however, there was more encouragement at Kilbeggan last time and he drops in class today so isn't dismissed.

RaceName: McCarthy's Irish Bar Lexington Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won over 3m at Limerick on return, her second chase win, but was poor at Wexford since and has to rebound; was disappointing on her only previous run here.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: 250-1 maiden hurdle winner two years ago; couple of decent runs in handicaps last year but form largely inconsistent; beaten 15l into fourth at Killarney (2m1f, good) 31 days ago over hurdles, staying on reasonably well from rear; beaten 21l over C&D in May; on a nice mark but needs to put best foot forward.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Six-time winner, including over C&D in a novice chase two years ago; form has been in and out over the last 12 months but best effort in that time came over C&D when 4.25l second off 4lb higher in May; below form last twice, pulled up at Wexford 47 days ago; on a good mark if return to this track sparks him up again.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Veteran who is 12-115 under all codes; five-time course winner, four times over jumps; dual C&D winner, latest 12 months ago off 7lb higher; much below best last two vists here but dangerous to completely write off in a winnable race at a venue he loves.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Three-time winner over hurdles, latest in October 2024; last two hurdle runs have been poor and was well-held 2lb higher in handicap chase at Roscommon in June; needs plenty more in first-time hood.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner last year who bounced back to form with second at Wexford (2m1f, good) in May; backed that up when beaten 6l into fifth at Listowel when out of the weights; below form when beaten favourite at Wexford lto; makes chase debut and appeals as the type with more to give.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: A 15-race maiden but her best form has come here; beaten 3.5l into third by well-handicapped rival over C&D in October off 7lb higher; below form three starts this term but she would have a big chance if reproducing October effort.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: A 14-race maiden but has had some good efforts, most notably when second at Punchestown (3m, good) in May off 4lb higher; well-held in four starts since and tries a shorter trip over fences; capable off this mark.

RaceName: Heinz Pollmeier Memorial Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Has been struggling in handicaps but ran one of his better races 13 days ago when keeping on to finish fifth at Cork (2m1f, good); needs fences to spark improvement.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Half-sister to some smart performers; showed ability when making late headway to be beaten 11.5l into fifth on debut at Killarney 31 days ago; hails from top yard; improvement expected and should be thereabouts.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Stepped forward with each of her three stars for Adrian Murray; 8l second to subsequent winner at Clonmel (2m4f, yielding) 124 days ago having raced with enthusiasm in the lead in first-time hood; looks solid form and drop in trip should help on stable debut; hood left off; leading player.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Didn't show a great deal in first three runs but much improved when beaten 4.5l into sixth at Sligo (extended 2m2f, good) 10 days ago; could be flattered by that however and needs to build on it.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Decent fourth over C&D on debut but followed up with poor effort at Cork; more like it last time when beaten 15.5l into seventh at Galway (extended 2m, good) keeping on; each-way shout.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: A 12,000euros foal; half-sister to Czech 6f 2yo winner Dantawi; unraced dam closely related to useful 7f/1m winner Akira, half-sister to 1m1f Flat/2m hurdle winner Halling Gal, out of unraced half-sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Husyan; bred to be sharp; yard gets bumper winners.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Slipped up when struggling on debut at Thurles; off 239 days; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: 3,000euros foal by Blue Bresil; dam unraced half-sister to winners Croco Bay (smart 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase) and Thistle Do Nicely (useful bumper and 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase); yard had bumper winner here in May.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: A 1,400 euros foal; dam unraced half-sister to 3m hurdle/chase winner Lunar Contact, out of unraced sister to Champion Bumper and smart 2m2f-2m4f hurdle/chase winner Briar Hill; decent pedigree and market can guide on debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Showed ability on debut when beaten 16l in good Galway bumper a year ago; backwards step when returned from long absence at Killarney 31 days ago, beaten 21l; market expected better; should come on for that and not to be dismissed based on debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Didn't complete in two point-to-points but outran odds when third past the post (demoted to fourth) at Galway 14 days ago; she was probably flattered by proximity but the first two are potentially smart so it was a positive effort; good chance here in winnable race.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Dam unraced half-sister to 2m chase winner Majorica King and French 1m7f hurdle/2m1f chase winner Six Fois Sept, out of Listed-placed 1m2f winner; market can dictate expectations on debut.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares INH Flat Race
Spotlight: Elusive Pimpernel mare; half-sister to point winner Break The Boundary; dam point winner, half-sister to 5f 2yo winner Cloudea; not an obvious type on paper to make a winning debut.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: From a good family and only modest effort came when when favourite for Lingfield Oaks Trial in the spring, but in decent form either side of that, following a second to Calasita in a Listed event (1m4f, good) in June with a Listed win at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) two weeks ago; stable in form.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Zarak half-sister to winners, chief among them Calandagan, and won two of her three starts over 1m4f, the most recent a Listed success from Romantic Symphony a couple of months ago on good ground, with the defeat coming behind Dispatches; holds Group 1 entries and capable of more improvement.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won twice as a 2yo and gone close in Listed, Group 2 and Group 1 company this campaign, her most recent run seeing her 3.25l fourth in the Prix de Diane (1m2f110yds, good to firm); anything like that sort of form on her first try at this trip (some stamina in her pedigree) would see her a leading player for this.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won three is a row, which included beating Calasita a length at Compiegne in May in a conditions race; hat-trick was landed in a Listed event at Longchamp (1m2f, good to soft) before being beaten by a top prospect at the same track in a Group 2 on first try over 1m4f; likely to be involved.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Kept some good company since winning here on the AW in November but has finished behind Dispatches the last two times they've met, including over this trip, so work to do with that rival.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Solid performer this season and not beaten far by some classy types following a couple of wins at the start of the year; close to her best in a 1m2f soft-ground Listed race at Vichy just over three weeks ago, and a good effort couldn't be ruled out.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Lady O'Reilly (Prix Minerve) (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Improved this season upped in trip, winning on her handicap debut at Ascot and picking up a 1m2f soft-ground Listed race on soft at Goodwood in June when cheekpieces were first tried; 50-1 and well beaten in the Ribblesdale Stakes (1m4f, good to firm) but may don better off a break and down in grade; likes to go from the front.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won on debut by 4l at this trip on soft ground and then picked up a Listed event here over 7f on the Round Course from the front when last seen a month and a half ago; that form looks solid and he might be hard to pass.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Debut winner at Newbury (6.5f, good to soft) before a step up in form to be fourth in a Group 2 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm); didn't build on that dropped into Listed company after but beginning to shape like a solid performer and should be thereabouts.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Only made debut in late June and not made much progress yet, although was beaten under a length over C&D a week ago; hard task to get first win in this race.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Won well on debut at York's Dante meeting (5f, good) and then went on to be fourth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); not so good in the Richmond Stakes after but can forgive a modest effort at Goodwood; enough in pedigree to suggest 7f won't be a problem if bouncing back.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Francois Boutin (Group 3) (Turf)
Spotlight: Supplemented for this; holds Group 1 entries and made a winning debut at Doncaster just over three weeks ago (7f, good to firm) from a colt who won next time; could be anything.

The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: 3-5 and turned in a clear pb to win the French 2,000 Guineas in May; failed to match that over 7f on quick ground behind Thesecretadversary in the Jean Prat but that proved his effectiveness on a sound surface and the form was franked when stable companion Samangan won the Maurice de Gheest; interesting back at 1m.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Unraced at two but created a fine impression last year, winning all four starts, including a convincing defeat of subsequent Group 1 winner Opera Ballo in the Joel Stakes; yet to match that form but not far off best when winning Group 2 at Ascot last time (better placed than More Thunder in a steadily run race); big chance back up in grade.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Disappointed in the 1,000 Guineas but bounced back to win the Irish equivalent and followed up in the Coronation Stakes; creditable second to Blue Bolt in both the Falmouth and Rothschild; tends to lose ground at the start but likely to go well getting the fillies' allowance on this first run against the boys.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Prolific winner with a fine strike-rate on AW and not far off pick of that form when beating subsequent dual winner Seagulls Eleven over this trip on a sound surface at Saint-Cloud in May; disappointed when last behind Zeus Olympios on most recent start and he has something to prove at this level.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Group 2 winner at Newbury last summer who posted solid efforts in Group 1 company on next three starts; failed to confirm Queen Anne placings with Zeus Olympios in steadily run Summer Mile at Ascot last time and he'll likely go well, especially if the gallop is honest.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
OwnerName: Cayton Park Stud & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Held in both the English/Irish 2,000 Guineas and best form has been around 7f but does stay this trip and has shown improved form to win the Jersey and Group 1 Jean Prat on last two starts; may find one or two too strong back over this trip, though.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Group 3 winner at this venue nearly a year ago and better than ever judged on reappearance win at that level at Saint-Cloud in spring; not seen since but, although he handles a sound surface, his two best efforts (by some way) have both been on ground described as soft.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Improved performer this year and registered first Group win when making all at Baden-Baden in June; hasn't been seen since and will find it harder to dominate in this company.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Did well to win - given he took a strong hold - a valuable Listed event at Abu Dhabi in February (July Cup wiinner Comanche Brave in third, Group 2 scorer Quddwah in fourth); long way below that level at Sha Tin last time and needs to return to his best.

RaceName: The Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois (Group 1) (Turf)
Spotlight: Has a good strike-rate and turned in best effort when bagging first Grade 1 over this trip on fast ground at Tokyo in June; not far behind the pick of the Europeans on that evidence and could be overpriced.

IFAHR CUP HANDICAP STAKES 0-95
Spotlight: Was narrowly beaten into second in this race last year but has gone from strength to strength since then; has won both his starts comfortably this season the most recent in May over a furlong further than this; has changed ownership and trainers since that run, he goes well fresh and if returning in the same form holds solid claims. (R9 W2 P6) (OR 76)

RaceName: IFAHR CUP HANDICAP STAKES 0-95
Spotlight: Stout stayer, who won this race last year when he made all the running. Was pestered on the lead at Lingfield last time when behind Ash'jaa but gets a big pull in the weights here; an easy lead looks likely here so should give it a good go from off the front.  (R21 W3 P8) (OR 72)

RaceName: IFAHR CUP HANDICAP STAKES 0-95
Spotlight: Made an impressive debut under this rider when winning at Lingfield last month, where he won by fourteen lengths in a weaker race than this; the extra furlong here on his handicap debut shouldn't be an issue, gives weight all round against some horses with solid form here, but he has obvious claims. (R1 W1 P0) (OR 88)

RaceName: IFAHR CUP HANDICAP STAKES 0-95
Spotlight: Finished fifth in this race last year but was ahead of Jeewan on her only start at Bath in the Spring; she's out of the weights here but has become very well treated nowadays, so she can't be discounted getting weight all round. (R14 W1 P8) (OR 64)(15oh)

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Won three C&D handicaps last year, including the corresponding race (ridden by Becky Smith) off today's mark; comes here on the back of a hat-trick of hurdle wins this summer; high on the list.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Chased home Stellarmasterpiece in this race last year having won a 1m2f amateur riders' handicap at Pontefract 12 days earlier; repeated his win at Pontefract 12 days ago and he should be in the thick of it again.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Just one win to his name since June 2023 and he has found it tough going so far in 2026; he has slipped a long way in the weights though and today's drop in class will help; not discounted.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark for the season when winning a 1m2f handicap at Doncaster 16 days ago, suited by the strong pace; 3lb higher mark to contend with and his stamina isn't assured.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: 9lb lower than for his Hamilton win last summer; struggling for form so far this season, however, and others bring more pressing claims.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field in two turf handicaps this summer after a five-month absence; on a dangerous mark but there are risks attached; blinkers replace cheekpieces today.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice over 1m2f last month (good and good to firm); pulled his chance away when third to Mariner at Doncaster 16 days ago; stamina for 1m4f has to be taken on trust but Henry Callan is 5-7 for James Owen and he should give it another good go.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: K Shenton, N Bradley 6 & D Cunha
Spotlight: Better efforts since a gelding operation, fourth in a 6f Southwell novice and a Class 5 nursery at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; drops into a Class 6 and could still have a bigger run in him.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Didn't run badly when third dropped back to 6f at Ripon three weeks ago without suggesting this sharper track would be ideal; she was caught out wide there though and the second has won since so she can't be discounted dropping into a Class 6.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Of interest on her best maiden/novice form but well short of that level on her last three starts (in cheekpieces on last two occasions); makes her belated nursery debut and should find this easier; well drawn to attack.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Some promise on her debut at Bath (5.7f, firm) but no impact in two subsequent runs; this should be more realistic and she is bred to be much better than a Class 6 operator; potential big improver.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Chased home a subsequent winner when second of six on nursery debut at Chepstow (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces first time) last month; drawn widest but still a solid contender with further progress possible.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field in three novice/maiden runs at up to 7f; faces a more realistic assignment on this nursery debut; betting to guide.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Shaped well on her debut at Ripon (6f, good) in May but that hasn't been a springboard to better things; never dangerous on her nursery debut last month; dropped 2lb and her trainer is banging in the winners.

RaceName: Well-Earned Retirement Neal Kidd Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Modest form in five starts, failing to improve for the switch to nurseries at Lingfield (5f, good to firm) last month; improvement required.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: Multiple C&D winner, including this race back in 2021; well drawn to attack but he is yet to fire in 2026; now back in the care of Ann Duffield.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
OwnerName: Eric Broadwith And Mrs Ruth Carr
Spotlight: This mark isn't beyond her but her style of racing doesn't really lend itself to this track; others appeal more for win purposes.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden; two fair runs for his new stable and he can win races off this mark; led last time but that won't be easy in today's field.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: In good form over 7f, winning at Wolverhampton in June and placed at Carlisle and Catterick since; Ethan Tindall takes off a handy 5lb; drop in trip not ideal but this looks likely to be run at a strong pace.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: Ran on well when winning a 6f handicap at Redcar in May; well held at Pontefract last month but that was in Class 5 company; 4lb lower than for her win in this race in 2024; should go well.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: Prominent racer; beaten favourite in two 5f handicaps on fast ground this summer but he has still run with credit; stays 6f but still seeking a first win at the trip.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: Front-running wins at Thirsk and over C&D last month; only fourth behind Miss Rainbow here 13 days ago but he used up a lot of energy getting to the front from the widest stall; better drawn today and he should have a big run in him.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins this summer, the latest over C&D 13 days ago when having a bit to spare; a 4lb higher mark may prove less of a hindrance than the widest stall.

RaceName: Chapman Milestones Celebration, Thank You NHS Handicap
Spotlight: All his wins have come over 5f, the latest at Hamilton in June (good to firm; cheekpieces first time); mixed bag since and although returning to Class 6 company will help, he may prove vulnerable to stronger stayers.

RaceName: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten favourite in three of his last four starts, including C&D; peak efforts give him a chance but not a compelling option.

RaceName: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Five-race maiden; beaten at odds-on at Windsor two weeks ago (tongue tied first time) having made the running; not progressing but she looks to have been found another good opportunity to break her duck.

RaceName: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: As with stablemate Star Noir he has claims on his best form, namely a 7f third at Musselburgh (soft) last November; two heavy defeats in handicaps this year and drops back to 5f on a recovery mission.

RaceName: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showed ability but ran to just a modest level in two 6f AW runs in January; hooded for her return to action; not bred to appreciate 5f but this is uncompetitive and she is open to improvement.

RaceName: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: David Tate, Danny Lawson & Kevin Broadley
Spotlight: Half-sister to winners Intrinsic Bond (5f/6f including AW; RPR 107), Instant Bond (6f including AW; 67), Billy Wedge (6f/7f AW; 66) and Premiership (1m; 64); dam unraced half-sister to 5f-7f winner Sea Salt; stable not known for winning newcomers but pedigree means she's worth a second look.

RaceName: Constant Security Services Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Mrs Michele Craig & Miss Linda Perratt
Spotlight: Second foal; dam 5f turf/6f AW winner (RPR 82), half-sister to Argentinian Group 1-placed 1m-1m4f winner Hat Valiente, out of Argentinian 7f Group 1 winner; makes belated debut for a stable not associated with winning newcomers.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
Spotlight: Wins his share and he got off the mark for the year over C&D last month; well held at Thirsk three days ago but in a Class 4; this should be more suitable.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
Spotlight: She is enjoying a good campaign and today's return to Class 5 company is in her favour; she has run well over C&D in the past and a big run looks on the cards from a handy draw.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
Spotlight: Won a C&D handicap off this mark last May; close third at Ripon three weeks ago but that was a lowly 0-55 handicap; more required in this field.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
OwnerName: Jimmy Kay, Tom Goodair And Grant Tuer
Spotlight: Saw off 16 rivals when winning a 5f handicap at Nottingham (good) in decisive fashion in April; soft ground was a valid excuse for a lesser effort at Yarmouth one month later (gelded after); sold for 10,000gns since; still has low mileage and he's of obvious interest against exposed rivals.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
Spotlight: Returned to action with a win at Nottingham (5f, good) in April and she ran a cracker at Beverley one month later; not so good twice since and a lower draw would have been preferred.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
OwnerName: J A Swinburne & Mrs Ruth A Carr
Spotlight: Started his campaign with two wins in April and there have been plenty of solid runs since; should remain competitive but minor money perhaps his best hope.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
Spotlight: Strong favourite when winning over C&D (good ground) in May; only 1lb higher today but that win came in a 0-55 and this is more demanding; others look stronger

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
OwnerName: R M Brilley, A E Townsend & Partner
Spotlight: Goes well around a left-hand bend; unlikely to have things his own way up front but he has the abiliity to win races off this mark.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins for his former stable, the latest at Hamilton (6f, good) in June; sold for 11,000gns last month; widest stall to overcome on his stable debut; a hood now returns.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
OwnerName: Ingleby Bloodstock Ltd & The Ivy League
Spotlight: Two of his four wins have come over C&D, the latest in June off a 2lb lower mark; come up short in two Class 4 runs since; not discounted back down in grade.

RaceName: racingtv.com Handicap
OwnerName: Grange Park Racing VIII & Mrs R Carr
Spotlight: Got off the mark on turf at Musselburgh in June; not so good twice since and he has a double-figure draw to defy this time.

RaceName: Racing Again 26th August Handicap
Spotlight: Beaten 16 times since a Dundalk maiden win in October 2024; series of good runs this summer, including tried in blinkers at Ayr last week, but he has work to do with Runninsonofagun on that evidence.

RaceName: Racing Again 26th August Handicap
Spotlight: Six wins this year, including his last four starts; coped well with the return to 5f at Hamilton last month but the return to 7f won't hurt; now moves out of Class 6 company but can't be discounted in current form.

RaceName: Racing Again 26th August Handicap

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: 30,000gns yearling; fourth foal; Havana Grey filly; dam unraced half-sister to two useful French winners; trainer also runs the twice-raced Andaman Fifty who has been placed.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Made a promising debut at Sligo, taking the runner-up spot despite betraying inexperience; got going too late at Cork and appears held by Stooked; both fillies are likely to appreciate the extra furlong.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Last of five at Killarney on belated debut; never in serious contention at Galway.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Made a promising debut when beaten a head by a more experienced rival at the Curragh, form upheld by the winner in landing a handicap at Gowran; probably found 6f inadequate when runner-up at Cork only six days later; almost sure to be in the mix.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Third foal; Churchill filly is closely related to Kashel Spring who won twice for Joseph O'Brien last year.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Frankel filly started her career with a fifth placing in a 1m Leopardstown maiden in which the subsequent Oaks winner Thundering On was second; again fifth in a 1m2f maiden at the same venue, beaten 9 1/2l behind the Irish Oaks Johanna Walsh; not much improvement in evidence at Naas on third start.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Has finished towards the back at Fairyhouse and Naas; can be left out of calculations.

RaceName: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
Spotlight: Has shown nothing in three outings in recent months; can be ruled out.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Uneven form this season; good third at Gowran before no show at Fairyhouse; bounced back with a close second at Dundalk before heavy defeat at Galway on latest; not the easiest to predict, could go well if in the mood.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Beaten 2.75l on debut at the Curragh by Thenandnow and 6lb better off with that rival here; got off the mark in a Navan maiden on latest (6f, good); rather speedily bred so whether this trip will suit is up for debate; cheekpieces go on.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Won a maiden at the Curragh in April (6f, soft); soundly beaten in Listed company on next two starts but back to form when a close third in a fillies' handicap at Fairyhouse (6f, good); not as good over 7f latest and stamina to prove for this trip.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: 9yo a winner of seven races; won twice last season at the Listowel Festival on heavy ground and has shaped encouragingly on last two starts at Limerick and Galway; rain would boost claims.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Four-time AW winner is 1-23 on turf; ran well at Bellewstown and Naas earlier this season but way below best the last twice at Leopardstown & Galway; others arrive in better form.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Has improved for handicaps; won off 7lb lower at Fairyhouse (7f, good) and another solid effort off revised mark when a close fourth at Naas on latest; can give another good account but very wide draw not ideal.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner; knocking on the door in recent starts; beaten 2.5l when third at Galway on latest; runner up over C&D in May off 2lb lower; frame claims again, especially if it rains.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
WTW Willis Handicap
OwnerName: Nigel O'Hare & Martin W White & Mark Devlin & C G Bryson
Spotlight: Two wins at the Curragh this season, both over 7f on good ground; not a bad run off revised mark over 1m there on latest and probably has more improvement to come but tricky draw to contend with here.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden winner over 6f last year; mixed bag so far this term; ran a cracker off this mark when beaten a neck at Naas (7f, good) last month; didn't back that up over 6f back there 15 days ago when upset in stalls; needs to rebound.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Narrowly denied at Fairyhouse in May (7f, good) and again at Limerick in June (7f, soft); bombed out when failing to beat a rival in a 3yo handicap at Leopardstown last time, however, so comes with risks attached.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Gained second career win off 5lb lower at Killarney in July (1m, good); has come up short twice since and has a bit to prove off his current mark.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Well backed and found just one too good on handicap debut at Gowran 11 days ago; 3lb rise for that pleasing effort negated by rider's 5lb claim; could go one place better now.

RaceName: WTW Willis Handicap
Spotlight: Handicap debutante has shown ability in maidens at 7f-1m; beaten just 2l when third in a Killarney maiden on seasonal return last month and ought to be up to winning races off her current mark; drawn wide but not discounted.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Reportedly green and lugged left throughout when beaten 4.75l on debut at Leopardstown (1m1f, good); however, he did finish off his race well and he's bred to relish this longer trip; enters calculations.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Beaten just a head on debut at Cork in April (10.5f, good) when sent off the 9-4 favourite; no excuses when beaten 2.25l upped to 1m4f at Leopardstown by now 95-rated rival; had subsequent maiden winners behind that day and he should be on the premises again.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Slow away and beat just one rival home on debut at the Curragh in June; Shane Foley jumps ship; others hold more pressing claims.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Not a bad effort when fourth on debut at Dundalk in May and similar RPR when last of six at the Curragh on latest; will qualify for handicaps after this.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner has run excellent races in defeat on his first two starts on the Flat; was only 1.5l behind Eagle Fang at Killarney and he has since run a huge race off 90 in the valuable Q.R. handicap at Galway; has to concede weight to most of these but big chance.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: 125-1 and never landed a blow on debut at Leopardstown 12 days ago; safely held by Magnum Cor on that run.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: 3yo filly shaped with promise on soft and soft to heavy ground at Gowran and Cork in the spring; below par on good ground at Killarney on latest; rated 77 and gets all the allowances but could probably do with some rain.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Tailed off in a German Group 2 and beat just one rival on Irish debut at Down Royal (1m5f, soft); hard to fancy but yard did win this with a 200-1 shot in 2023.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Failed to beat a rival when 33-1 on debut at Ballinrobe; may need a bit more time.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Huge odds and soundly beaten in maidens at Killarney and Gowran; handicaps beckon after this.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Triple-figure odds for both starts and ran accordingly; will be of more interest when tackling handicaps.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Ordinary form over jumps in Britain and tailed off on sole previous Flat start on AW; not easy to make a case for on Irish debut.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Has shown virtually nothing in four maidens at around 1m on a variety of ground; upped in trip and cheekpieces now tried.

RaceName: District Speciality Coffee Maiden
Spotlight: Heavy defeat on debut at Gowran; beaten 17l when last of 11 at Cork on latest; leap of faith required to back her after those two runs.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: 0-8 last year for Willie McCreery; modest enough start for this yard when beaten 14.5l at Gowran (13.5f, soft); eased 1lb and new headgear combination needs to spark.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
OwnerName: Athlumney Farms Ltd & Eoin Baxter & Mrs M D O'Callaghan
Spotlight: Sole success came in a 9.5f Ballinrobe claimer last summer; stays this far and should be sharper for latest modest third at Galway but probably hasn't got much in hand off current mark.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Six-time winner, most recently at last year's Galway festival over 7f (yielding) off 12lb higher; below best so far in 2026 and stamina a major query on first run beyond 1m2f.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Scored at Leopardstown (1m1f, gd-fm) in June off basement mark; hiked up 10lb and beaten just 1l back at Leopardstown before staying on well at Gowran on latest (9.5f, good); worth another go at this trip on that evidence; chance.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Likeable front running veteran goes well here; last won over C&D in May 2025 off this mark and was beaten a neck in this race last year, again off this mark; showed he retained ability when second at Fairyhouse in May; trip was too far on latest, could make a bold bid.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: No impact in first two runs for this yard; tailed off on latest at Galway and, while likely capable of better, can only be watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Best effort came over 10.5f in an AW maiden; hasn't figured in first two handicaps but did shape okay in a C&D maiden in mid-May; eased 3lb for 6l defeat at Naas on latest, rider takes off further 5lb and cheekpieces go on; interesting.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Not the easiest to win with (1-30) but often runs well in defeat; poor efforts on last three starts, however, and needs to get back on track; yard form a positive.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner last May off 11lb lower; hinted as though returning to form when an encouraging third at Killarney but then clipped heels and unseated at Galway; likes it here and could go very well.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden has a race in her and she didn't enjoy the smoothest of passages when catching the eye at Galway last time; eased 1lb and if the forecast rain materialises it would boost her prospects.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Handicap debutante has shown promise in all three maidens at 1m1f-1m5f on varying ground; opening mark may be workable and not discounted, especially if money comes.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Won a bumper here last year (2m, good); best run this year came over C&D when a 5l sixth and 4lb lower now; decent run over hurdles at Kilbeggan 10 days ago; place claims if the forecast rain misses.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Modest form so far in three maidens at 1m4f-1m6f (including over C&D) and when tailed off in a bumper; bred to do better at some stage so worth a market check on handicap debut.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Both previous turf wins have come over 1m but landed a 1m4f handicap at Dundalk in February; eased 4lb for midfield finish at Galway last time and worth checking in the market.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Versatile sort won over hurdles at Listowel in June but has failed to fire in that sphere twice since; returns to the Flat in a first-time visor; others arrive in better form.

RaceName: Class Grass Handicap
Spotlight: Won twice on the Flat last year including over C&D off 5lb lower; two runs this term not his best and may need some more help from the handicapper; won't mind if there's rain.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Promising third of 11 on debut at Kempton (1m, AW) in March; absence since is a slight concern but otherwise he holds fair claims.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beat only one home on debut at Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) last month; drops back in trip on AW debut and should know more this time.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Never competitive after starting slowly when seventh of 12 on debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in April; has had wind surgery since so she may step up.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Promising second of four on debut at Chelmsford (7f, AW) last November; she makes a belated return to action but the booking of Oisin Murphy may be significant.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Beaten over 17l when fourth of five on debut at Yarmouth (1m2f, good to firm) 13 days ago; has a lot of improvement to find.

RaceName: Download The At The Races App EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: R J Manning & Mrs Fiona Williams
Spotlight: Beat only one rival in her two races on turf last year; first-time cheekpieces are applied on AW debut; best watched.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Third foal; out of a 1m3f-1m4f AW winner (RPR 89); satisfactory start to his career when fourth to  more experienced rival at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm; 13-2) 16 days ago; likely to know more on this occasion.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-brother to the frequent scorer Oj Lifestyle (7f-1m2f; RPR 92); clear encouragement from opening effort when fifth of 12 at Southwell (7f; 20-1) three weeks ago; should progress and have a role to play.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 25,000euros yearling; some promise when sixth on Southwell debut (6f; 17-2) in July when beaten 8l; half-brother to six winners, including the milers Whispering Bell (RPR 90) and Stardayz (81), so the extra furlong is worth exploring.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Nick Bradley Racing 6 & Hold My Beer
Spotlight: 42,000euros yearling; weakened to finish last of 12 on last week's Kempton debut (7f; 40-1); this swift turnaround is another part of the learning curve; others more obvious.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 8,000gns foal, 38,000gns yearling; second foal; out of a 7f winner (including AW; RPR 89); already gelded but, with Oisin Murphy booked (1-3 for the yard in the last five seasons), he merits market scrutiny and consideration for a trainer operating a 13% juvenile strike-rate in 2026 (2-15 on AW).

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 20,000gns yearling; modest late headway when beaten about 10l on Southwell debut (6f; 28-1) four weeks ago; moves up in trip, with Hector Crouch taking over in the saddle; stablemate of Brazilian Blitz.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Slowly away and failed to figure in either start at 7f and 1m; her dam was a lightly raced half-sister to the Group 2 winner Nyaleti (1m), but this one looks like she'll need more time; handicaps await soon.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 26,000gns yearling; fourth foal; out of 5f winner (RPR 96); half-brother to two winners, principally Ange De L'Amour (6f 2yo; 72); stable aren't a regular source of winners in these events, and he's already gelded; monitor only.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Slowly away and always behind on Kempton debut (7f; 28-1, beaten 21l) in late June; this half-brother to the 7f AW-1m2f turf winner Titanium is poorly drawn and likely to need more time; look elsewhere.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 28,000gns breeze-up purchase; dwelt and ran green throughout on last week's Kempton debut (7f; 40-1) when beaten 13l; hard to consider as a viable contender on that evidence.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Few positives to take from AW runs at Newcastle and Southwell (both 7f); will soon be eligible for a handicap mark; unlikely today.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Weakened to finish last of nine on Yarmouth debut (7f, good to firm; 80-1) 16 days ago; switches to AW but no real reason why he should get closer to Javelot (fourth) this time.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Shaped with a deal of promise on his first run at beyond sprint trips/handicap debut at Southwell three weeks ago, when not helped by the way the race panned out; will have learned more again from that and should go well.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Won her maiden on Tapeta and turned in her best effort of the year back on the AW over C&D late last month, when coming away with the winner/favourite; not as well drawn tonight and is 3lb higher but holds claims nonetheless.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
OwnerName: P C J Dalby & R D Schuster
Spotlight: Found the race not run to suit at Epsom early last month, when hanging left, but then pulled way too hard in front on his Tapeta debut latest; that was far from the first time he'd over-raced and much will hinge on how he settles early from the inside stall.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Generally struggled early in the year and returns from a break of five months; wins have all come after a recent outing and does most of his racing at a lower level now, so has a bit to overcome.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Missed more than 18 months prior to a few lesser efforts in the spring, but has found his level again; enjoyed the run of the race when winning narrowly on Polytrack last Wednesday but set to go well again under a penalty for a yard in good nick.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Three turf wins over a straight 1m for Edward Bethell as a 3yo, latterly off a 2lb lower mark, before struggling during a limited campaign last year; would need a career-best effort for his new yard (also responsible for Spaceman) back from 11 months off.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Winner here off 2lb lower last October, his third over C&D; last month's Chester comeback from a short break should have brought him on and he holds each-way claims under Oisin Murphy, who boasts a good record for the yard.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
OwnerName: A Pot To Pete In Syndicate
Spotlight: Dual Southwell winner off lower marks early in the year who ran poorly there when last seen and has been off for almost four months since; would need a career-best in order to take this.

RaceName: Visit wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk To Book Now Handicap
Spotlight: Dual 7f Polytrack winner in his younger days but does most racing now over 6f; made a poor debut in a claimer for his new yard here last month, having been picked up for 10,000gns from Richard Hughes last autumn; surprise to see him take this.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Placed on first start for this trainer at Southwell (1m; hooded) in April; hasn't kicked on since, but did emerge with a suitable excuse (lost both hind shoes) when a beaten 6-4 favourite at Nottingham (1m2f) latest; slowly easing mark.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Pounced to break her duck over C&D (beat Blue Celestial by half-a-length) on penultimate start; gave a good account of herself back on turf when second at Haydock (1m) subsequently; it's likely she'll be in the mix again with Rose Dawes retaining the ride.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Uplift for fitting of a hood (absent tonight), and a switch to handicap company; lacked pace when third at Sandown (1m2f, good to firm; 12-1) four weeks ago; dropping back to 8.5f isn't the most obvious play, but she's on the same mark.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 12-race maiden; some consistent efforts though, losing out narrowly on her last two starts, including to Sunshine And Roses over C&D; handicap mark continues to rise (up another 2lb) which won't make life easier; still merits respect.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Hasn't managed to beat too many rivals across four starts and was last of seven on Ripon handicap debut (1m, good; 9-1) one month ago; now 2lb lower, with added cheekpieces, for AW return; tough to consider.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Mrs R Coleman And G Glendining
Spotlight: Runner-up at Kempton (1m; 11-4 favourite) on penultimate start, and didn't get the breaks at Windsor (1m) subsequently; has a few foibles - unseated rider in the paddock at Newmarket - but she's still a possible from 2lb above last winning mark.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: The Hon Heather Galbraith & C Maxwell
Spotlight: Gave willingly to brush off a 5lb penalty at Musselburgh (1m1f, good) 11 days ago; steps up in grade (from 4lb higher) in pursuit of the hat-trick for an in-form trainer; no issue with this track, so obvious claims with Oisin Murphy aboard.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Not many positives to take from her efforts in novice/maiden company, 'the pick' a never dangerous fourth of ten at Pontefract (1m2f; 40-1) in early July; AW switch, and visor, could yield improvement on handicap debut.

RaceName: Surestore Self Storage Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 0-8; weakened late when runner-up over 9.5f here (12-1) in May; has regressed race by race since; returns to AW in added visor with plenty to prove.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Ridden positively for two 6f Newcastle wins and found the race not panning out to suit under a more patient ride upped to 7.2f here a month ago; back on her last successful mark and should fare better.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
OwnerName: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
Spotlight: Newly gelded; had excuses with one thing and another this year; this mark looks within range and there are positives back on the AW, and under Oisin Murphy, who boasts a decent record for the yard; shortlisted.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Bath blowout in the spring can be ignored but he started a big price when last of seven on his return from a break a fortnight ago; while the return to the AW may do the trick, others hold stronger claims.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive on the AW last winter, winning three times, latterly off tonight's mark; the return to Tapeta and drop back from 7f will help, with the visor experiment quickly binned, but he hasn't been in any form in three runs back from a break.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Consistent maiden who's proved competitive in handicaps this season without looking to have anything in hand, or anything left in the way of improvement; still has each-way claims coming back up from 5f.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Found an ordinary 5f handicap when making all at Leicester (first-time cheekpieces) in early summer; put up a harsh 8lb for that, didn't back up the effort next time and has been off for seven weeks since; needs more on his AW debut.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Won his maiden over C&D in February, since when he's been turned over four times as favourite in handicaps; last two efforts, including one having been gelded, were particularly poor, and leave him plenty to prove; stable in fine form, though.

RaceName: Maggies Handicap
Spotlight: Beat Percy's Star when easily winning his maiden on turf in the spring; difficult to know what happened on his handicap debut off 2lb higher late last month, but possible he needed that and it's still early days.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: Steadily progressive stepping up in trip and got off the mark at the fifth attempt, at Sandown (1m6f, good) in June; wasn't able to handle the step up in class at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) last month when fifth of seven but holds obvious claims back on AW at this level.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
OwnerName: D Bevan And Mrs D Bevan
Spotlight: Took advantage of a career-low mark and return to Southwell AW, where he had shown his best form previously, to get off the mark last month; 5lb higher and holds claims if able to reproduce his best at this different track.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: All six wins have been on AW, the latest over C&D last November off 3lb lower; not so good on turf but was runner up at Carlisle (1m6f, good) last Tuesday which holds her in good stead for this return to AW.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: Versatile sort whose four wins have all been at this track between 1m4f to around 2m; well-handicapped on his best form but hasn't won for 12 months and some of his younger rivals may have more scope.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: Sole success came in a Kempton AW handicap in July last year when trained by Tom Ward; had an unsuccessful stint over hurdles this year for current yard, and well held in a couple of 2m handicaps since; drops back in trip on AW return and best watched for now.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
OwnerName: C Wright, D Kilburn, A Dick And P Snook
Spotlight: Ended last season with two slow-ground wins on turf from the front (1m2f/1m4f); safely held twice on good ground this year (1m4f/1m2f) and needs to show more on this step up in trip on AW return.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: 11l second to a subsequent Royal Ascot flop in novice at Kempton (1m3f, AW) on debut in May; has finished last in both starts on turf since and return to AW on handicap debut needs to show him in a better light.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: Has shone since reverting to handicaps, winning twice here (1m4f) and he completed a four-timer at Newbury (15.5f, good to firm) last month; no disgrace in finishing second to a fellow improver at Sandown (1m6f, good to firm) last time and looks sure to be thereabouts.

RaceName: Self Storage Association Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins came at this track (1m4f) at the end of last year; runner-up in a couple of turf handicaps since, but was below his best when fifth of eight at Sandown (1m6f, good) last month; the return to this track may see him in a better light.
